narrative:
The model estimated a 90 percent chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because law school admission here is tied to likely bar success, that high predicted risk is why your application was denied. The decision is not a judgment of your ability; it reflects the pattern in the records reviewed.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing. You are in the lowest tenth of your class, while accepted students average around the sixth tenth; this pushed the prediction toward failure more than any other item. Your LSAT result was the second strongest factor: 19.30 versus an accepted-student average of about 37.18, also pushing toward failure. Your first-year class standing was the third most influential factor: lowest tenth versus an average near the sixth tenth, again pushing toward failure. Other information, such as your middle-income background and full-time status, mattered less.

To move forward, ask admissions for feedback, strengthen your academic record where possible, prepare carefully for and consider retaking the LSAT, seek academic support, and apply again when your evidence better shows readiness for bar success.
